- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.3) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by forecast overshoot, apply downward correction of 3–5% in subsequent days.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.1) and model forecasts are high, reduce forecast by 2–4% to align with mean reversion bias.
- Model often underestimates prices in early forecast horizon (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is neutral or slightly positive — adjust upward by 1–3% for first 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is volatile or mixed (0.1–0.3), model tends to lag behind true price — apply 1–2% upward bias for next 3–5 days.
- For long-term forecasts (15+ days), model often underestimates upward trends — add 1–2% cumulative adjustment if sentiment remains positive.
- If sentiment is rising sharply (e.g., >0.4 over 3 days), model tends to overreact — cap forecast at 1–2% below recent peak.
- If model consistently forecasts lower than true price in 30-day window, apply 1–3% upward adjustment for next 5–7 days, especially if sentiment is neutral or positive.
